tagline: A blasted wagon-road passage links Sierra ridges, lakes and Carson Pass.
intro: Highway 88 climbs the Sierra Nevada along a ridge, with overlooks into river canyons, then descends rapidly east of Carson Pass toward Hope Valley. Its mountain section belongs to California’s State Scenic Highway System and is designated a National Forest Scenic Byway. The western climb separates the North Fork Mokelumne watershed from a succession of watersheds to the north.

A toll-road franchise granted in 1852 aimed to fund a replacement for the old route between Tragedy Spring and Caples Lake. That wagon road had looped past Silver Lake and crossed a ridge near Emigrant Lake at 9,640 feet. Crews blasted a new passage through Carson Spur in 1863 and widened it with further blasting in 1960. Another realignment moved the eastern approach from Red Lake’s south shore to its north side. It lengthened the climb but reduced the grade, changing the approach to the pass as well as the western crossing. Winter maintenance began in 1971 as Kirkwood’s resort developers agreed to provide facilities and contribute toward snowplowing.

Heading east, pass Silver Lake before the road drops through Carson Spur to Kirkwood, then climbs beside Caples Lake to Carson Pass. The descent has a viewpoint over Red Lake, reaches Hope Valley, and follows the Carson River through Woodfords Canyon into Carson Valley toward Nevada.

moments.title: Kirkwood
moments.text: Kirkwood’s log inn is a California Historical Landmark, connecting the town to travel before the ski resort. Cattle rancher Zack Kirkwood established the inn beside the Amador/Nevada Wagon Toll Road. It served travelers as an inn, post office and restaurant. The creation of Alpine County put the inn at the convergence of Alpine, El Dorado and Amador counties, though later boundary changes altered that arrangement. Its interior includes a mahogany bar, timber furniture and a stone fireplace fitted with a gas insert. The mountain resort opened in 1972, after Caltrans began year-round snowplowing on Highway 88 in 1971.

moments.title: Carson Pass
moments.text: Carson Pass crosses the Great Basin Divide, between the West Fork Carson River to the east and the South Fork American River to the west. In 1848, Mormons leaving California for Utah built the Carson Trail through the pass, linking Sly Park and Carson Valley. It became a major Gold Rush route. The crossing also carried Civil War shipping to California until completion of the first transcontinental railroad. The Pacific Crest Trail crosses the summit. A marker records where Kit Carson carved his name into a tree in 1844; the original carving is at Sutter’s Fort in Sacramento.

moments.title: Woodfords
moments.text: At the mouth of Woodfords Canyon, Highway 89 leaves Highway 88 and turns toward Markleeville. An earlier name, Brannan Springs, recalled Sam Brannan, who left supplies beside a spring here in 1847 while traveling to Salt Lake City. Woodfords had an earlier, brief role in a different transport network: it became a Pony Express remount station on April 4, 1860. Rider Warren Upson arrived from Lake Tahoe by Luther Pass during a snowstorm, then continued toward Carson City. Five weeks later, the Pony Express switched to Echo Summit and Kingsbury Grade. The remount station is designated California Historical Landmark 805.

practical: Carson Pass: Caltrans attempts to keep Highway 88 open year-round, but Carson Spur closes periodically for winter avalanche control. (checked 2026-10-11)
